verifier_validation.restamp_note: Fingerprint re-stamped 2026-07-26 WITHOUT re-labelling: its definition widened to cover the evidence template, which was extracted from an inline f-string. The rendered evidence is byte-identical — pinned by tests/test_surface.py::_check_evidence_renders — so these labels were collected against the same characters the judge sees now. A change to what the judge is SHOWN (not just how it is stored) does require re-labelling.
verifier_validation.invalidated: 7 of the 37 cases were judged on the wrong number — _provenance handed the judge a breakdown's FIRST row instead of the row the answer served (e.g. V027/V029 t2_paid_search_spend_q2: judge shown 10643.22, answer served 36875.98). The blind sheet carried the same wrong `query_result`, so the human labels were formed against it too. Both sides of the comparison used corrupted evidence, so the 92% agreement / 6% miss / 10% false-flag rates below do not describe the judge as it now runs.
verifier_validation.next_step: Re-draw a blind sample from a post-fix R9 run and re-label; the rates above must not be quoted until then.
